name: GLB to VRM
description: One rigged humanoid GLB in, a VRM avatar out: automatic humanoid bone mapping, then VRMify writes a VRM 1.0 or 0.x avatar with MToon materials.
overview: GLB2VRM turns a rigged humanoid GLB into a VRM avatar. The skeleton is matched to the 22 VRM humanoid bones automatically — by bone name for known rigs (Mixamo, VRoid, Unity, Blender, HumanIK, 3ds Max Biped, MMD), and from the skeleton shape for generic rigs named bone_0…bone_21. Extra chains off the hips (a tail, skirt or cloth from an auto-rigger) are tolerated: the spine is recovered from the hips path that carries the arms. Blender then imports the mesh and exports an FBX with the mapped bone names, VRMify's own converter builds a PMX model and writes the VRM (1.0 by default, 0.x optional), and the result is validated against the official VRM JSON schema. The returned avatar keeps its textures and materials as MToon. Drop a rigged humanoid GLB on the canvas, select that 3D layer, choose the options, then Run.

parameters.name: input_mesh
parameters.label: Rigged Humanoid GLB
parameters.description: A rigged humanoid .glb with an armature. The selected 3D layer is uploaded here automatically.

parameters.name: tpose
parameters.label: T-Pose
parameters.description: Raise A-pose arms to the VRM T-pose.

parameters.name: spring
parameters.label: Spring Bones
parameters.description: Add hair, skirt and ribbon chains from bone names.

parameters.name: tex_max
parameters.label: Texture Size
parameters.description: Downscale texture atlases. 0 keeps the original size.

parameters.name: tex_jpeg
parameters.label: JPEG Textures
parameters.description: Store opaque textures as JPEG to shrink the VRM.

parameters.name: face180
parameters.label: Face 180° Flip
parameters.description: Turn the avatar around when the facing detection comes out backwards.
